paragraphs.title: Creation as a Royal Garment and Cosmic Order

answers: As very great and clothed with honour and majesty
easy.explanation: Psalm 104:1 says, “O LORD my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe the LORD at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The LORD is described as covering himself “with light as with a garment” (verse 2).
easy.q: What is light compared to?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says that he “stretchest out the heavens like a curtain.”
easy.q: What does the LORD stretch out like a curtain?

medium.explanation: The passage presents light, heavens, clouds, winds, and fire as parts of the ordered creation under God’s rule.
medium.q: Which group of images expresses the LORD’s rule over creation?

answers: A vehicle or means of riding
medium.explanation: The clouds are pictured poetically as the LORD’s chariot.
medium.q: What is meant by “his chariot” in “who maketh the clouds his chariot”?

answers: They display his activity and authority
They are described as his enemies
They prevent the earth from being formed
medium.explanation: The LORD rides upon the clouds and wind, and his angels and ministers serve him as spirits and fire.
medium.q: How are the clouds, winds, and fire related to the LORD?

answers: Creation is presented as an ordered royal setting under God’s rule
Nature is shown as completely disordered
Human beings are described as rulers of heaven
challenge.explanation: Both images portray creation as something beautifully arranged and associated with divine majesty.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by the images of light as a garment and the heavens as a curtain?

answers: The earth is full of riches
God’s angels are spirits and his ministers a flaming fire
Man goes forth to his labor
challenge.explanation: Verse 4 explicitly calls them God’s angels and ministers.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the powers described are servants rather than independent forces?

answers: It presents different parts of creation under one divine ruler
It describes only human daily life
It explains only the limits of the sea
challenge.explanation: The sequence moves through several cosmic elements, all presented as subject to God’s authority.
challenge.q: How does the sequence from light to fire support the main idea?

paragraphs.title: The Foundation of the Earth and the Boundaries of the Waters

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “Who laid the foundations of the earth.”
easy.q: What did the LORD lay as the foundation of the earth?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “At thy rebuke they fled.”
easy.q: What happened to the waters at God’s rebuke?

answers: To the place founded for them
easy.explanation: The waters go to the place that God has founded for them (verses 7–8).
easy.q: Where do the waters go after moving over the mountains and valleys?

answers: Mountains and valleys appear, and the waters are assigned a place
medium.explanation: The waters move over the mountains and valleys and are confined to the place appointed for them.
medium.q: What is the result of the waters retreating?

answers: A fixed limit that cannot be crossed
medium.explanation: A bound is a limit; the waters may not pass over it.
medium.q: What does “bound” mean in “Thou hast set a bound”?

answers: The LORD has set them a boundary
medium.explanation: Verse 9 says that God set a bound so that the waters would not return to cover the earth.
medium.q: Why can the waters not cover the earth again?

answers: The waters flee, revealing mountains and valleys
challenge.explanation: The waters retreat at God’s command, and the mountains and valleys are revealed in their appointed places.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between God’s rebuke and the shape of the land?

answers: The permanence of the waters’ boundary
The lack of control over nature
challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses that the waters will not return to cover the earth.
challenge.q: What does “that they turn not again to cover the earth” emphasize?

answers: The earth is established and the waters are limited to their appointed place
The earth and waters mix without boundaries
Human beings alone establish the order of the world
challenge.explanation: The earth is made firm, while the waters remain within the limit God assigned.
challenge.q: How is order portrayed in this passage?

paragraphs.title: Water as the Source of Life for Plants and Animals

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says that the springs run “among the hills.”
easy.q: Where do the springs run?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says the springs give drink to every beast of the field.
easy.q: Who receives drink from the springs?

easy.explanation: Verses 14–15 describe grass, herb, food, wine, oil, and bread.
easy.q: What does God cause to grow from the earth?

answers: They give animals drink and make plant growth possible
medium.explanation: The springs give drink to animals, while the rain and waters nourish the hills and earth.
medium.q: How do the waters help both animals and plants?

answers: The high places or storehouses from which water comes
medium.explanation: The phrase poetically pictures God’s heavenly storehouses supplying water to the hills.
medium.q: What are “his chambers” in “He watereth the hills from his chambers”?

medium.explanation: The earth produces grass and herbs, and food and bread strengthen human beings.
medium.q: Which sequence describes the earth’s provision for human beings?

answers: They provide habitats for many kinds of creatures
They are intended only for human beings
challenge.explanation: The passage describes trees, mountains, and rocks as homes and refuges for different creatures.
challenge.q: What does the mention of birds, wild goats, and conies show about water and vegetation?

answers: God waters the hills, and the earth is satisfied with the fruit of his works
The earth does not need water
challenge.explanation: Verse 13 says that God waters the hills and that the earth is satisfied with the fruit of his works.
challenge.q: How is the relationship between rain and the earth described?

answers: Bread results from the earth’s growth and provides strength to man
challenge.explanation: The earth produces food, and bread is described as strengthening human beings.
challenge.q: What is the connection between bread and the other gifts of the earth?

paragraphs.title: The Cycles of Time and the Lives of Humans and Animals

easy.explanation: Verse 19 says, “He appointed the moon for seasons.”
easy.q: What did God appoint the moon for?

easy.explanation: Darkness becomes night, “wherein all the beasts of the forest do creep forth” (verse 20).
easy.q: When do the beasts of the forest come forth?

answers: He goes forth to his work and labor
He searches for prey in the forest
easy.explanation: Verse 23 says, “Man goeth forth unto his work and to his labour until the evening.”
easy.q: What does man do after the sun rises?

answers: They mark the cycles of time
medium.explanation: The moon is appointed for seasons, and the sun has its appointed going down and rising.
medium.q: What roles do the moon and sun have in this passage?

medium.explanation: When the sun rises, the animals gather together and lie down in their dens.
medium.q: What does “their dens” refer to in the passage?

answers: Animals act at night, retreat when the sun rises, and man goes to work
Man works at night while animals work during the day
Both animals and humans sleep all day
medium.explanation: Verses 20–23 describe this sequence of night activity, morning retreat, and human labor.
medium.q: What is the order of activity from night to morning?

answers: Night suits the forest animals, while daytime suits human labor
Both humans and animals work only at night
Time has no connection with activity
challenge.explanation: The passage assigns nighttime activity to the beasts and daytime labor to man.
challenge.q: How does the cycle of day and night divide activity between animals and humans?

answers: The fitting relationship among the heavenly bodies, animals, humans, and time
Only the size of the sea
challenge.explanation: The coordinated order of creation prompts the declaration, “in wisdom hast thou made them all.”
challenge.q: What leads the psalmist to marvel at the wisdom of creation?

answers: All the cycles of life and time are part of a wise creation
Only the sun was made wisely
challenge.explanation: The statement summarizes the ordered relationships among the earth, its creatures, and the passage of time.
challenge.q: What does “in wisdom hast thou made them all” mean in this context?

paragraphs.title: The Sea, Its Creatures, and Leviathan

easy.explanation: Verse 25 calls it “this great and wide sea.”
easy.q: How is the sea described?

easy.explanation: The sea contains innumerable creeping things and beasts, both small and great.
easy.q: What is found in the sea?

easy.explanation: Verse 26 says, “There go the ships.”
easy.q: What moves across the sea besides its creatures?

answers: That the sea has literal hands
medium.explanation: The expression emphasizes the broad extent of the sea.
medium.q: What does “great and wide sea” emphasize?

answers: As a creature made by God and under his control
As an independent ruler of the sea
medium.explanation: Verse 26 says that Leviathan is one whom God made to play therein.
medium.q: How is Leviathan presented in the passage?

answers: The variety of sizes among the sea creatures
The absence of life in the sea
medium.explanation: The phrase highlights the sea’s abundance and variety.
medium.q: What does “both small and great beasts” emphasize?

answers: Even a mighty creature remains under God’s authority
challenge.explanation: The image places even the enormous Leviathan within God’s creative purpose and control.
challenge.q: What is suggested by describing Leviathan as made to play in the sea?

answers: It is an ordered, life-filled realm governed by God
It is a place without order
It is separate from God’s activity
challenge.explanation: The sea, its creatures, ships, and Leviathan all belong to the world God has made.
challenge.q: How does the sea fit into the psalm’s larger picture of creation?

answers: A sense of immense abundance and variety
A distinction between good and evil
challenge.explanation: The contrast suggests countless creatures of many different sizes.
challenge.q: What effect is created by the contrast between “small” and “great”?

paragraphs.title: All Creatures Depend on God’s Sustenance

easy.explanation: Verse 27 says, “These wait all upon thee.”
easy.q: To whom do all the creatures look for their food?

answers: The creatures are filled with good
The earth is covered with water
easy.explanation: Verse 28 says, “thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good.”
easy.q: What happens when God opens his hand?

answers: Creatures are created and the earth is renewed
The animals return to their dens
easy.explanation: Verse 30 says, “Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth.”
easy.q: What happens when God sends forth his spirit?

answers: His provision enables the creatures to gather food and be filled with good
medium.explanation: God gives the creatures their meat, and they are filled when he opens his hand.
medium.q: What is the connection between God’s provision and satisfaction?

answers: They depend on and look to God
medium.explanation: The creatures wait for God to provide their food in due season.
medium.q: What does “wait all upon thee” mean?

answers: The creatures are troubled, die, and return to dust
medium.explanation: Verse 29 describes trouble, death, and return to dust when God withdraws their breath.
medium.q: What happens when God hides his face and takes away their breath?

answers: Receiving from God, living, dying, returning to dust, and being renewed
Death without any possibility of renewal
challenge.explanation: The passage includes both death and return to dust and the creation of life through God’s spirit.
challenge.q: What cycle of life is described in this passage?

answers: All wait for his food, and he determines their life and renewal
challenge.explanation: The passage speaks of all creatures waiting for God’s provision and receiving life from him.
challenge.q: How is every creature’s dependence on God presented?

answers: Death and renewal are two stages in the cycle of life
challenge.explanation: The passage places return to dust alongside the renewing work of God’s spirit.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between returning to dust and renewing the face of the earth?

paragraphs.title: The Psalmist’s Praise and the Psalm’s Conclusion

easy.explanation: Verse 31 says, “The glory of the LORD shall endure for ever.”
easy.q: How long shall the glory of the LORD endure?

answers: Sing unto the LORD and sing praise to God
easy.explanation: Verse 33 says, “I will sing unto the LORD as long as I live.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist promise to do during his life?

answers: Bless thou the LORD, O my soul. Praise ye the LORD.
Thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good.
Man goeth forth unto his work.
easy.explanation: The final words are, “Bless thou the LORD, O my soul. Praise ye the LORD.”
easy.q: With what words does the psalm end?

answers: The animals returning to their dens
medium.explanation: The psalmist says that the LORD rejoices in his works and declares, “I will be glad in the LORD.”
medium.q: What causes the psalmist to rejoice in the LORD?

answers: The psalmist’s thoughts and words of praise about God
medium.explanation: The psalmist says that his meditation of God shall be sweet.
medium.q: What does “my meditation of him” refer to?

answers: The ending returns to the call to bless the LORD
medium.explanation: The psalm begins and ends with an exhortation to bless the LORD.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the beginning and ending of the psalm?

answers: They respond to his power by trembling and smoking
challenge.explanation: The LORD looks upon the earth and it trembles; he touches the hills and they smoke.
challenge.q: How do the earth and hills in the conclusion reinforce God’s greatness?

answers: A desire for evil to be removed from the earth
A desire to increase the power of the wicked
A request to restore the night
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks, “Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more.”
challenge.q: What does the request concerning sinners and the wicked express?

answers: It joins God’s enduring glory and joy in creation with a desire for evil to disappear
It describes only the food of animals
It cancels the cycle of life
challenge.explanation: The ending combines praise for God’s works with a prayer that sin and wickedness will no longer remain.
challenge.q: How does the conclusion connect with the earlier theme of renewal?
